items.statement: Among higher-confidence reviews, professional interpretation is consistently associated with better patient-reported understanding than ad hoc interpretation, while no higher-confidence review supports equivalence of video and in-person interpretation for understanding.
items.rationale: Separates the supported and unsupported parts of the committee's decision (c1, c2, c3).

items.statement: Accounting for overlap reduces the apparent number of independent studies supporting professional interpretation by more than half.
items.rationale: Overlap was substantial in the methods study (c3).
items.risks: Overlap calculation depends on complete reference lists.

items.statement: Tested bilingual staff perform closer to professional interpreters than untested staff on error rates.
items.rationale: Informs whether the standard can include tested bilingual staff.

summary: Three propositions; h1 organises the overview's main comparison.
